Aspleniaceae.key_door: Asplenium resiliens: narrow 1-pinnate frond + glossy black axis + linear sori with one-sided true indusia + clathrate scales

Polypodiaceae.key_door: Pleopeltis michauxiana: creeping epiphytic rhizome + peltate lower-blade scales + round naked sori + resurrection response

Thelypteridaceae.key_door: Thelypteris kunthii: terrestrial pinnate-pinnatifid frond + transparent hairs/glands + round sori + hairy reniform indusia

anchor_families.Pteridaceae: local cliffbrake framework: marginal sori under rolled blade margin acting as a false indusium

taxonomy_notes: Asplenium resiliens, Pleopeltis michauxiana, and Thelypteris kunthii are accepted current species concepts.
Current Kew treats Pleopeltis polypodioides var. michauxiana as a synonym of accepted Pleopeltis michauxiana.
Family circumscription conflict is explicit: Flora of North America retains Thelypteridaceae as a separate family, while Kew 2026 synonymizes Thelypteridaceae into a broad Aspleniaceae.
The project retains Thelypteridaceae as a labeled regional teaching family rather than silently changing the 147-family project universe in this batch.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Teach fern family differences from sori, indusia, scales/hairs and growth architecture, not generic frond shape.
Do not hide the Kew/FNA family-circumscription disagreement.
Do not call Pleopeltis epiphytism parasitism.
